intended_object: The canonical k-algebra homomorphism kQ → Π_k(Q) from the path algebra of a finite quiver Q to its (additive) preprojective algebra. It sends each path of Q to the class of the same path in the doubled quiver. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation, which cite Crawley-Boevey and Ringel.
explanation:
The body has two steps:
1. `mapAlgHom k Symmetrify.of _` is the algebra map kQ → k(Q̄) induced by the inclusion prefunctor `Symmetrify.of : Q ⥤q Symmetrify Q`. This prefunctor is the identity on vertices, hence bijective on objects, which is the hypothesis `mapAlgHom` needs to preserve the unit.
2. It is composed with `preprojectiveMk`, the quotient map k(Q̄) → k(Q̄)/(Σ[a,a*]), which is Π_k(Q).

This is exactly the standard map kQ → Π_k(Q). The library also proves the standard properties: it sends paths to their classes, and it has a retraction, so it is injective.

Generality is natural. k is an arbitrary commutative ring. The finiteness assumptions (finitely many vertices, finitely many arrows between each pair of vertices) are used by the library's path algebra, where the unit is a finite sum of vertex idempotents, and by the preprojective relator, which is a finite sum over arrows. These are the standard assumptions for this construction.

Mathlib has no path algebra or preprojective algebra, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
